\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ടെർമിനൽ} (ṭerminal)}{ടെർമിനൽ (ṭerminal)}]{\ml{ടെർമിനൽ} (ṭerminal) — a terminal}

\label{lesson:ML-C463-terminal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to make a booking, then the Malayalam for to buy a ticket.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ടെർമിനൽ}}
\textbf{\ml{ടെർമിനൽ}} — \emph{ṭerminal} — \textquotedblleft{}a terminal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വിമാനത്താവളത്തിൽ} \ml{രണ്ട്} \ml{ടെർമിനലുകൾ} \ml{ഉണ്ട്}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vimānattāvaḷattil raṇṭŭ ṭerminalukaḷ uṇṭŭ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The airport has two terminals.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ml{ടെർമിനലുകൾ}, \emph{ṭerminalukaḷ}.

Plural: add -\ml{ഉകൾ}, as for most loans that end in a chillu.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ടെർമിനൽ}} (\emph{ṭerminal}) was borrowed from English \emph{terminal}, a building where journeys begin and end.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭerminal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭerminal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimānattāvaḷattil raṇṭŭ ṭerminalukaḷ uṇṭŭ.} — The airport has two terminals.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to make a booking, then the Malayalam for to buy a ticket, then say \emph{ṭerminal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ടെർമിനൽ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A terminal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{റൺവേ} (ṟaṇvē)}{റൺവേ (ṟaṇvē)}]{\ml{റൺവേ} (ṟaṇvē) — a runway}

\label{lesson:ML-C463-ranve}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to buy a ticket, then the Malayalam for a terminal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{റൺവേ}}
\textbf{\ml{റൺവേ}} — \emph{ṟaṇvē} — \textquotedblleft{}a runway\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വിമാനം} \ml{റൺവേയിലൂടെ} \ml{വേഗത്തിൽ} \ml{ഓടി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vimānaṁ ṟaṇvēyilūṭe vēgattil ōṭi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The plane ran fast along the runway.
\end{quote}

The ending -\ml{ലൂടെ} means along or through: \ml{റൺവേയിലൂടെ}, along the runway.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{റൺവേ}} (\emph{ṟaṇvē}) was borrowed from English \emph{runway}, the strip where planes land and take off.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṟaṇvē}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṟaṇvē}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimānaṁ ṟaṇvēyilūṭe vēgattil ōṭi.} — The plane ran fast along the runway.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to buy a ticket, then the Malayalam for a terminal, then say \emph{ṟaṇvē} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{റൺവേ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A runway\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{വിമാനക്കമ്പനി} (vimānakkampani)}{വിമാനക്കമ്പനി (vimānakkampani)}]{\ml{വിമാനക്കമ്പനി} (vimānakkampani) — an airline}

\label{lesson:ML-C463-vimanakkampani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a terminal, then the Malayalam for a runway.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വിമാനക്കമ്പനി}}
\textbf{\ml{വിമാനക്കമ്പനി}} — \emph{vimānakkampani} — \textquotedblleft{}an airline\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ആ} \ml{വിമാനക്കമ്പനിയുടെ} \ml{ടിക്കറ്റിന്} \ml{വില} \ml{കുറവാണ്}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā vimānakkampaniyuṭe ṭikkaṟṟinŭ vila kuṟavāṇŭ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That airline's tickets are cheap.
\end{quote}

Literally a plane company: \ml{വിമാനം}, a plane, plus \ml{കമ്പനി}. In the joined word the -\ml{ം} of \ml{വിമാനം} drops and the \ml{ക} of \ml{കമ്പനി} doubles.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{വിമാനക്കമ്പനി}} (\emph{vimānakkampani}) is a Malayalam compound built from \ml{വിമാനം}, a plane, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{vimāna}, a car of the gods that moves through the air (CDIAL 11823), and \ml{കമ്പനി}, which was borrowed from English \emph{company}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimānakkampani}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimānakkampani}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā vimānakkampaniyuṭe ṭikkaṟṟinŭ vila kuṟavāṇŭ.} — That airline's tickets are cheap.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a terminal, then the Malayalam for a runway, then say \emph{vimānakkampani} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{വിമാനക്കമ്പനി} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An airline\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{പറന്നുയരുക} (paṟannuyaruka)}{പറന്നുയരുക (paṟannuyaruka)}]{\ml{പറന്നുയരുക} (paṟannuyaruka) — to lift off; to take off}

\label{lesson:ML-C463-parannuyaruka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a runway, then the Malayalam for an airline.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പറന്നുയരുക}}
\textbf{\ml{പറന്നുയരുക}} — \emph{paṟannuyaruka} — \textquotedblleft{}to lift off; to take off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വിമാനം} \ml{കൃത്യസമയത്ത്} \ml{പറന്നുയർന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vimānaṁ kṛtyasamayattŭ paṟannuyarnnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The plane took off on time.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{പറന്നുയർന്നു}, \emph{paṟannuyarnnu}.

Two verbs joined: \ml{പറന്ന്}, having flown, and \ml{ഉയരുക}, to rise. Landing is \ml{ഇറങ്ങുക}, to come down.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{പറന്നുയരുക}} (\emph{paṟannuyaruka}) is native Dravidian, a compound of \ml{പറക്കുക}, to fly (DEDR 4020), and \ml{ഉയരുക}, to rise: the plane flies and rises.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṟannuyaruka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṟannuyaruka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimānaṁ kṛtyasamayattŭ paṟannuyarnnu.} — The plane took off on time.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a runway, then the Malayalam for an airline, then say \emph{paṟannuyaruka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{പറന്നുയരുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To lift off; to take off\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ട്രോളി} (ṭrōḷi)}{ട്രോളി (ṭrōḷi)}]{\ml{ട്രോളി} (ṭrōḷi) — a luggage trolley}

\label{lesson:ML-C463-troli}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for an airline, then the Malayalam for to lift off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ട്രോളി}}
\textbf{\ml{ട്രോളി}} — \emph{ṭrōḷi} — \textquotedblleft{}a luggage trolley\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വിമാനത്താവളത്തിൽ} \ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{ബാഗുകൾ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{ട്രോളിയിൽ} \ml{വച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vimānattāvaḷattil ñān bāgukaḷ oru ṭrōḷiyil vaccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At the airport I put the bags on a trolley.
\end{quote}

A shopping trolley in a supermarket is a \ml{ട്രോളി} too.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ട്രോളി}} (\emph{ṭrōḷi}) was borrowed from English \emph{trolley}, a cart on wheels for bags.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭrōḷi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭrōḷi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimānattāvaḷattil ñān bāgukaḷ oru ṭrōḷiyil vaccu.} — At the airport I put the bags on a trolley.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for an airline, then the Malayalam for to lift off, then say \emph{ṭrōḷi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ട്രോളി} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A luggage trolley\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
